[[File:Foragebushes prev aoe2.png|200px|right]]'''Berry Bushes''' or '''Forage Bushes''' are an early [[food]] source and appear in every game of the [[Age of Empires (series)|series]]. == {{1icons||36}} ==

{{quote|Can be foraged for food.|In-game description in the ''Definitive Edition''}} The '''Forage Bush''' and '''Fruit Bush''' (or '''Berry Bush''' before ''[[Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition - Return of Rome|Return of Rome]]'') in ''[[Age of Empires]]'' provides an easily-accessible, naturally-occurring source of food, making it a key resource from the [[Stone Age]] to early [[Tool Age]]. Each Bush yields {{resources|food = 150}}, which can be deposited at the [[Granary (Age of Empires)|Granary]] or [[Town Center (Age of Empires)|Town Center]]. Note that foraging and farming are the only resource types that [[Villager (Age of Empires)|Villagers]] cannot deposit at the [[Storage Pit (Age of Empires)|Storage Pit]]. Villagers gather food from foraging at a moderate rate: far slower than [[Fishing|fish]]ing and, since the ''[[Age of Empires: Definitive Edition|Definitive Edition]]'', slightly slower than [[hunt]]ing. However, it is still faster than the gathering rate of [[Fishing Boat (Age of Empires)|Fishing Boats]]/[[Fishing Ship (Age of Empires)|Ships]], and on par with [[Farm (Age of Empires)|farming]]. The key advantage is that Bushes are so easy to harvest: unlike fish, they typically occur in large clusters; unlike land animals, they are stationary, so do not require micromanagement-intensive herding or luring strategies; unlike farming, they require no wood or construction time. For these reasons, foraging is often the main source of food in the early game. Bushes can't be reseeded, making them a finite resource. Typically, easily-accessible sources are depleted quite early in the game. This is where Farms come into the picture, as they can always be replaced whenever a sufficient supply of [[wood]] is available. Foraging was originally solely from Berry Bushes, but ''Return of Rome'' replaced them with Forage Bushes and Fruit Bushes, carried across from ''[[Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition]]''. With the release of ''[[Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition - The Last Chieftains|The Last Chieftains]]'', the '''Pineapple Bush''' and '''Papaya Tree''' were also added to ''Return of Rome''. {{-}} == {{2icons||36}} ==

Like its predecessor, the '''Forage Bush''' in ''[[Age of Empires II: The Age of Kings|Age of Empires II]]'' provides an early source of food. Forage Bushes always appear in clusters, and there is usually a cluster near every player's starting [[Town Center (Age of Empires II)|Town Center]]. Building a [[Mill (Age of Empires II)|Mill]] nearby helps increase collection rates by minimizing the time Villagers need to spend walking to their drop-off points. On most maps, there are several other Forage Bush clusters scattered around the map. Each Bush contains {{resources|food = 125}}. It is advisable to gather food from animals first before gathering from Bushes since the working speed of [[Villager (Age of Empires II)#Gathering rates|foragers]] is slower, at {{Resources|food = 0.31}} per in-game second. However, foraging is still faster than farming when taking into account the fact that they do not need to walk around nearly as much, and foraging does not require a wood investment outside of building a Mill or [[Settlement (Age of Empires II)|Settlement]] near the Berry Bushes. Most random maps have players start near 6 Forage Bushes, for a total of {{resources|food = 750}}. However, some maps start with alternate amounts; [[Scandinavia]], [[Hill Fort (map)|Hill Fort]], and [[Greenland]] feature no Forage Bushes near players' starting positions, [[Yucatán (map)|Yucatan]] has 12 bushes per player, and [[Budapest]] has 6 for each ''Town Center'' rather than player. In ''[[Age of Empires II HD: The African Kingdoms|The African Kingdoms]]'', the '''Fruit Bush''' was introduced. It only differs from the Forage Bush in its appearance. Similarly, in ''[[Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition - The Last Chieftains|The Last Chieftains]]'', the '''Pineapple Bush''' and '''Papaya Tree''' were introduced. === Civilization bonuses === * {{2icons|Aztecs}}: Foragers carry {{resources|food = +3}}. * {{2icons|Franks}}: Foragers work {{tt|15%|25% before Lords of the West}} faster. * {{2icons|Gurjaras}}: Start with 2 Forage Bushes with {{Resources|food = 175}} each. * {{2icons|Mapuche}}: Foragers drop off {{Resources|food = {{tt|+25%|+20% before update 177723}}}}. * {{2icons|Mayans}}: Forage Bushes last {{tt|15%|20% before The African Kingdoms}} longer. * {{2icons|Portuguese}}: Foragers generate wood in addition to food ({{resources|wood = 0.33}} per food). {{-}} == {{Micons||36}} == {{Infobox resource |Name = Berry Bush |Image = AoMR Berry Bush icon.png|Retold AoM Berry Bush icon.png|Original |Intro = {{Micons}} |Food = {{tt|150|100 before Retold}} }} {{quote|Villagers tasked on edible crops will gather Food.|In-game description}} The Berry Bushes in ''[[Age of Mythology]]'' contain {{resources|food = {{tt|150|100 before Retold}}}}, and like in the other games, clusters of them can sometimes be found close to the [[Town Center (Age of Mythology)|Town Center]]. They are gathered by [[worker]]s {{tt|at the same rate as from [[Farm (Age of Mythology)|Farms]]|approx. 14.5% faster before update 18.27100; worker-specific ratios before Retold}}. They are a slow, but safe method of gathering food, but are quickly depleted. As such, the player must turn to other sources of food by the mid-game. In ''Retold'', Berry Bushes spawn typically in a ring with enough space for food drop site buildings inside. Certain god powers can destroy Berry Bushes. Those include [[Wither]], [[Locust Swarm]], [[Inferno#Norse|Inferno]], and [[Divine Slash]]. In [[Arena of the Gods]], the Blessing "Demeter's Berry Cultivation" not only makes workers gather food from Berry Bushes faster, but also makes it such that constructing a [[Granary (Age of Mythology)|Granary]], [[Ox Cart (Age of Mythology)|Ox Cart]], [[Manor (Age of Mythology)|Manor]], [[Silo]], [[Watermill]], or [[Calpulli]] spawns a Berry Bush next to it when completed. === God bonuses === * {{Micons|Ra}}: [[Laborer]]s gather food {{tt|30%|25% before update 19.14612}} faster from Berry Bushes. (since [[update 17.30764]]) === History === {{quote|Berry bushes symbolize the gathering nature of pre-agricultural humans and are a staple of Age of Empires games. Berries, like all fruit, evolved as a means for plants to disperse their seeds--in this case through the digestive tracts of animals.}} {{-}} == {{3icons||36}} ==

The ''[[Age of Empires III]]'' Berry Bush holds {{Resources|food = 1,000}} and is harvested by [[Settler (Age of Empires III)|Settlers]], [[Villager (Age of Empires III)|Villagers]], [[Coureur des Bois]], [[Cree Coureur des Bois]], or [[Settler Wagon]]s. The Berry Bush, unlike animals, do not lose food over time due to decay, but the gather rates are slower (the same as a [[Mill (Age of Empires III)|Mill]], except for the [[French (Age of Empires III)|French]]). Berry Bushes usually come in clusters of 2-4, and last a considerable amount of time to European and Asian civilizations. Most maps usually have a cluster of berry bushes near them as an early source of food. They should not be used by the French Coureur des Bois, or those utilizing Cree Coureur des Bois due to the fact both units gather berries slower than working at a Mill. Furthermore, major Native American civilizations should always use hunting (spawning new animals as the [[Lakota]], or [[Haudenosaunee]] via [[Home City Card|cards]]), fishing, and berries for as long as possible due to the inferiority of the [[Farm (Age of Empires III)|Farm]] to berries, Mills, and fishing. In the ''Definitive Edition'', [[Torp]]s constructed will spawn a Berry Bush. However, these Berry Bushes only hold {{Resources|food = {{tt|200|150 before update 13088, 125 before update 14825}}}} and decay over time. With the "Blueberries" [[Home City Card]], Torps will spawn a Blueberry Bush, which have {{Resources|food = +200}} and are gathered twice as fast by Torps, instead of a Berry Bush, and turns all Torps' Berry Bushes into Blueberry Bushes. Blueberry Bushes also appear in the [[Scandinavia]] map included with the ''[[Age of Empires III: Definitive Edition - Knights of the Mediterranean|Knights of the Mediterranean]]'' expansion. {{See Also|[[Food#Gather rates]]}} === History === {{quote|There are many varieties of berries native to the Americas. Tart cranberries grow in cranberry bogs, flooded at harvest time to float the ripe berries to the surface where they are skimmed off and dried or put into preserves. Thorny blackberry bushes grow wild in the southern United States. The Guarana berry grows in the northeastern parts of South America and is named after the Guarani tribe.}} {{-}} == {{4icons||36}} ==

{{Quote|Use Villagers to gather Food from this forage bush.|''Age of Empires IV'' description for the Berry Bush}} In ''Age of Empires IV'', Berry Bushes contain {{Resources|food = 250}} and have a standard gather rate of {{Resources|food = {{tt|0.69|0.66 before update 12.0.1974}}}} per second. They usually appear in 'medium' or 'large' groups of six and eight respectively, with one of these groups almost always near the [[Capital Town Center]], and several more groups around the map. More rarely, they can also appear in 'small' or 'straggler' groups of two bushes, on which maps these groups usually spawn in greater number and more evenly distributed around the map. The [[Abbasid Dynasty]], the [[Ayyubids]], and the [[Delhi Sultanate]] can create orchards by constructing a [[Mill (Age of Empires IV)|Mill]] near Berry Bushes, improving their capacity to {{Resources|food = 350}}. They also gather from them 25% faster, at {{Resources|food = 0.8625}} per second. The [[Twin Minaret Medrese]] [[landmark]] for the [[Ottomans (Age of Empires IV)|Ottomans]] spawns up to four renewable bushes with an improved 50% gathering rate on them. [[Byzantines (Age of Empires IV)|Byzantine]] Villagers also generate {{Resources|olive oil = +50%}} when gathering from Berry Bushes. On the Greek Islands [[biome]], Berry Bushes are replaced by Prickly Pear Bushes, despite the latter being native to the Americas and not introduced to Southern Europe until after the Middle Ages. They are identical other than their model. == Trivia == * The berries throughout the ''Age of Empires'' series appear to be based on either redcurrants or raspberries, both which are common throughout the Old World and the Americas. The species of the fruit bushes are unknown, although it is plausible they could be gooseberries. ** The Fruit Bush could also be based on ''[[wikipedia:Strychnos spinosa|Strychnos spinosa]]'', a bush or tree with yellow fruit that is native to Africa. However, the fruit on ''Strychnos spinosa'' is round in shape, while the Fruit Bush's fruit is closer to a lemon shape. ** The fruits may be lemons, as lemons are widely cultivated fruits (originating as a hybrid cultivar of bitter orange and citron) and were present throughout the Old World. Moorish North Africa (represented by the Berbers in-game) was one of the channels for the spread of lemon cultivation to the Iberian peninsula during the time period of ''Age of Empires II''. ** Citron, another candidate for identity of the yellow fruit, was known to African populations as early as the 15th century BCE. Evidence suggests citron was cultivated at Karnak during the reign of Pharaoh Thutmose III. The word ϭⲓⲧⲣⲉ means "lemon" or "citron" in the Coptic language (the liturgical language of the Coptic Orthodox Church, dating to early Christendom). * Since the presence of Berry Bushes is something of a running joke in the [[Age of Empires (series)|''Age of Empires'' series]], the Berry Bush description in ''Age of Empires III'' reads "It wouldn't be ''Age of Empires'' without berries". * ''[[Age of Empires III]]'' and ''[[Age of Empires IV]]'' are the only games in the series which feature technologies that improve the berry gathering rate. Prior to ''[[Age of Mythology: Retold|Retold]]'', this was true of ''[[Age of Mythology]]'' as well. However, ''Retold'' does feature two effects which improve berry gathering rates: a [[major god]] bonus for [[Ra]] and a Blessing in the [[Arena of the Gods]] game mode. * According to the prototype data entries, other food-based plant sources were planned to have been added in ''Age of Mythology'', according to the Multiplayer Alpha language.dll file and WildCrops tag. == Gallery == Foraging.gif|A Forager harvesting a Berry Bush in ''Age of Empires'' AoEDE Berry Bushes.png|Foragers harvesting Berry Bushes in ''Age of Empires: Definitive Edition'' Foragers.png|Foragers harvesting a Berry Bush in ''Age of Empires II'' Fruitbush.png|Fruit Bushes in ''Age of Empires II'' Villager berrybushanim aoe2de.gif|A Forager harvesting berries in ''Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition'' Papaya and Pineapple views AoE2DE.png|Papaya and Pineapple in ''Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition'' AoM Berry.png|Berry Bushes in ''Age of Mythology'' Aomr berry bush gather.png|Laborers gathering from Berry Bushes in ''Age of Mythology: Retold'' Holidaze berry and chicken.png|Pumpkin model of the Berry Bushes in the "Holidaze Event" (November 25–December 22, 2024) in ''Age of Mythology: Retold'' Berry Bush aoe 3.png|Berry Bushes in [[Ceylon]] in ''Age of Empires III'' Berry bushes ingame aoe3de.jpg|Berry Bushes in [[Araucania]] in ''Age of Empires III: Definitive Edition'' Berry bushes de scandinavia.jpg|A Berry Bush and two Blueberry Bushes in [[Scandinavia#Age of Empires III|Scandinavia]] in ''Age of Empires III: Definitive Edition -
